summary: Atsushi Kiyozawa worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral course at the University of Delhi and held a lecturer post at Kindai University, attested in 1989.

Atsushi Uno specialized in Indology and philosophy, studying at Kyoto University, Banaras Hindu University, and under T. R. V. Murti and others. He held teaching posts at Kyoto, Shuchiin, Tokai, Hiroshima (professor, 1974–1986), and Kindai University.

Atsuuji Ashikaga worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After graduating from Doshisha and Kyoto University, he served as professor and dean at Kyoto University (1930–1962) and later as honorary professor at Tokai University (~1967–1975).
Atsuyoshi Keika is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Otani University, where he served as lecturer (attested 1990) and professor (attested 2014).

August Boeckh specialized in history, archaeology, and linguistics. After studying under Wolf and Schleiermacher at Halle, he held academic posts at Heidelberg University (1807–1811) and the University of Berlin (1811–1861).

August Conrady worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. Educated at Würzburg and Leipzig, he taught at Peking University (1903–1904) and held posts at Leipzig University from 1891, becoming full professor of Sinology in 1920.

August Dillmann was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. He studied under Heinrich Ewald at the University of Tübingen and held academic positions at Tübingen, Kiel, Giessen, and the Frederick William University Berlin (1869–1894).
August Ferdinand Naeke studied at Leipzig University (~1805–1810). He later held posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg and the University of Bonn (~1818–1838).

August Fick specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Göttingen (1852–1856) under Theodor Benfey, later serving there as extraordinary professor (1876) and as ordinary professor at the University of Breslau (1887–1891).
August Fischer worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1886–1889) and held a post at Leipzig University (~1900–1930).

August Friedrich Pott specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Göttingen and under Franz Bopp in Berlin, lectured at Berlin, and was professor of general linguistics at the University of Halle from 1833.

August Hermann Francke was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at the Niesky teachers' seminary, Moravian Theological College, and Berlin, later becoming a Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1922.

August Hjalmar Edgren worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Uppsala, Cornell, and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Yale, Lund, the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (~1885–1901), and served as rector at Gothenburg (1891–1893).

August Johan Bernet Kempers was an archaeologist and Indologist. Educated at Leiden University (~1926–1933), he directed Dinas Purbakala (~1947–1953) and held posts at the Netherlands Open Air Museum (1958–1971) and University of Amsterdam (1969–1984).

Linguist August Leskien studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Jena under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He taught at Göttingen and Jena before serving as professor of Slavic studies at Leipzig University from 1870 to 1915.
August Rudolf Hoernle worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as director at Aliah University (~1881–1899) and was secretary of The Asiatic Society in 1891.

August Schleicher was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Bonn under Ewald, Ritschl, and Lassen. He held professorships at Charles University (1850–1857) and the University of Jena from 1857.

August Wilhelm Schlegel worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Göttingen under Heyne and Bürger, and later under Chézy and Hamilton. He was an extraordinary professor at Jena (1795–1801) and Bonn's first Indology chair from 1818.

Auguste Barth was an Indologist and scholar of religion who studied at the University of Strasbourg. He taught at Collège de Saverne (~1860–1870) and was a member of the Institut de France (~1893–1916).
Auguste Comte was a philosopher who completed his studies at Lycée Joffre until 1814 and at École polytechnique from 1814 to 1816.
